transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

I’m here because things at work have gotten… concerning. Ever since I got that county safety award, certain people have been twisting my inspection reports, and they keep asking these pointed budget questions like they’re trying to make me look crooked. My supervisor says it’s just normal review, but it doesn’t feel normal. I can tell there’s some kind of coordinated effort to discredit me.

Along with these concerns about being targeted at work, have you noticed any significant changes in your mood—like feeling unusually elated, energetic, or irritable, or on the other hand, very down or depressed?

I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve been stressed and frustrated about what’s happening at work, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been unusually up or energized, and I don’t feel depressed exactly. It’s more that I’m on edge because of the situation.

How long have you felt that people at work are coordinating to discredit you—did this start suddenly around the time of the award, or is this a pattern of feeling suspicious of others that you've noticed throughout much of your life?

It’s been about a year, I’d say. It really started after I got recognized for that county safety initiative. I wasn’t going around my whole life thinking people were after me or anything like that—this feels tied to what happened at work after the award.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that others couldn't hear, or seen things that others didn't see, during this past year?
No, I haven’t had anything like that. I don’t hear voices or see things other people don’t. It’s more about what people are doing and saying at work.
Aside from the situation at work, how have things been going in other areas of your life—like your relationships with family or friends, and your ability to manage daily responsibilities?

Outside of work, I’m mostly keeping up. I still get to work on time, finish my inspections, take care of myself, and I’ve been keeping up with church. Family and friends are… okay, I guess. The problems mostly start when people bring up those reports or start questioning how I’m spending my money. That’s when things get tense.

Besides feeling that people at work are trying to discredit you, have you had any other unusual beliefs—for example, that you have special abilities, a special mission, or that your thoughts or actions are being controlled by outside forces?

No, not like special powers or a mission or anything controlling me. It’s really about work. Since that county safety award, certain people have been twisting my inspection reports and asking these pointed budget questions like they’re trying to make me look crooked. My supervisor says it’s just normal review, but I can tell it’s more coordinated than that.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a well-systematized, non-bizarre persecutory delusion (belief that coworkers are coordinating to discredit him following a workplace award) persisting for about one year. There are no hallucinations, no disorganized speech or behavior, and no mood episode (manic or depressive) accompanying the delusional beliefs, ruling out schizophrenia and mood-related psychotic disorders. Functioning is preserved in most domains (work performance, self-care, religious involvement, relationships) except where it intersects with the delusional theme, consistent with Delusional Disorder rather than Schizophrenia, which requires broader functional decline and additional psychotic features. The circumscribed nature, absence of bizarre content, and preserved baseline functioning support F22 as the best-fitting diagnosis.
